rationale.complete: Rounds 1, 1b and 2 done: round 2 tested the Pólya urn (exponent predicted from composition), dilution vs address for kicks, trap depth as a model trait and the spell-kind mixture rival, with synthetic validation on the real skeletons first. Reserved data not used; content-level spirals not run.
rationale.faithfulness: Kramers core failed (round 1). Round 2 adds an intervention: the NE41 forced erasure inside a trap lifts #51 gate escape 0.47 -> 0.84 (log OR +2.68 [2.31, 3.16]), frailty-proof by synthetic check; the own-call urn predicts the gate-clock exponent unfitted (-0.36 vs -0.35) but not the wall-clock one; kicks work by address. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E2 F2 G1 H1 I1. The wall-clock exponent is not separable from day-level states (post hoc).
rationale.usefulness: Directly actionable: erase or consolidate the context of an agent that keeps re-pausing (84% vs 47% escape at the next gate in #51); name the agent when messaging (directed read +0.69 vs chatter +0.24 log odds); one message is enough. Exploratory, one long period.

one_line: Pause-chain traps are held by the context: a forced erasure ends most of them (0.47 -> 0.84), and a message works by naming the agent, not by diluting its repeats.

models.note: Kramers escape from a double well; traps age, and the trap state is held by the context window (erasure step)
Pólya urn on own repeats: predicts the gate-clock exponent from composition and absorbs half of it; fails on the wall clock, in tokens, and for kicks

v2.adjudication_note: Different claim scored: the coordinator scored a composite that included the withdrawn error-loop aging, framed it as 'power only in #51' (x0.6) and marked it fragile; the blind rater scored silence and pause-gate aging, which never changed between data versions. Ruling: score aging of silences and pause chains plus the one-kick gate effect, with the error-loop result excluded; fragile is false because the scored headline did not move (the error-loop collapse is a withdrawn sub-finding, per the clarification). Credence comes out where the rater put it, V is material for an operator.
